product.name: xmlsquish
product.description: A local-first, deterministic project manager and compiler for XML prompt projects.

cli.automationMigration: Existing public CLI and namespace remain unchanged; private derived identities may rebuild. Existing SOPack input bytes and SHA-256 lock pins remain immutable.

integrity.note: SHA256SUMS verifies downloaded bytes, not publisher identity. Binaries are unsigned and not Apple-notarized.

highlights: Full document/provenance/resource-directive identity for pack reuse.
Whole SOPack validation before referenced-unit compilation; strict local-source validation retained.
Verified immutable snapshots and borrowed/shared mechanisms retain integrity and durability checks.
Canonical ZIP direct validation and content/topology-based portable provider identity; hosted verification and performance conclusions pending.
Structured failures preserve exact relocated source records and actual invocation chains; cache-result rejection does not conflate derived CAS corruption with published-product corruption.
Repeated text content sharing preserves public string interfaces, per-selection provenance, logical byte budgets and diagnostic ordering; exact-source validation pending.

skills.integrity: BLAKE3 complete-tree digest; integrity does not establish trustworthiness

products.sopack: Reproducible ZIP compiled library without final products

compatibility.singleRelocatedRewrite: Preserve existing provider names and normalized bytes.
compatibility.freshProducerBuilds: Provider fingerprints may change across producer versions; no cross-version byte-identity promise.
compatibility.inputOwnership: Existing archive bytes and lock pins remain immutable.

verification.performanceClaims: Earlier scalar regressions and the passing 6b2a31b repair checkpoint are historical; subsequent text-sharing source requires exact hosted gates and measurements. No universal gain claimed.
verification.scope: Catalog preparation avoids derived CAS-output hydration but still verifies committed publications. Warm SOPack proof reuse is bound to exact frozen encoding digest and size, not arbitrary valid IR.
